missionPremise: G-151 builds the Parks lens into the shipped product as the one lens that does NOT exist, rendering the negative claim (there is nothing to read, why, and the one decision that would change it) on the clean side of the design's two-sided vocabulary rule, without registering the domain, without a metric tile, without an empty table, and without reaching for any of the three near misses that carry the word Parks. What the lane verified rather than assumed: the design is ratified and its instrument already self-tests in both directions; the three refusals are pinned in the product and are re-fired by the lens module rather than quoted; Parks is absent from DOMAIN_REGISTRY and stays absent; the artboard reader cannot reach built markup, so the --dir bridge is a second reader rather than a loosened first one; and the inherited RED test named in the dispatch was already fixed upstream at this branch's base.
completionPredicate: Three clauses readable by a stranger from artifacts rather than from this sentence: (1) the design instrument passes ON THE BUILT SURFACES with non-zero matched-input counts printed (bodies=5, badges=6, cells=134, fonts=258, roster=20, builtOnContrast=8) and refuses 11 of 11 planted violations, including refusing a VERDICT on the renamed scope marker rather than failing it; (2) the shipped surface is scanned AS A FILE and carries no table, no metric tile and none of the 9 built-surface vocabulary terms, with the composer sentence verbatim, and the scan itself is shown failing on three planted copies; (3) node --test exits 0 (895/895) and the three parks-facilities probes still refuse, quoted. The fourth clause - the DO reach - is FAIL and named as needing a merge plus a planner-owned deployment.
scopeBasis: In scope: src/parks-lens.mjs and its test (new), src/server.mjs's GET /lens/parks route, web/index.html's Parks section, and four new scripts (bake, export, probe, prove-refusals); plus the design instrument's --dir reader (uncommitted in doc_repo). Out of scope and untouched: src/domains.mjs / DOMAIN_REGISTRY (the row's central prohibition), src/adapters.mjs, the six other lenses' modules, web/app.js, every data-lens-* attribute name, every design dump, and every deploy and merge.
falsifier: What would falsify this close: (a) an instrument that passes with a ZERO matched-input count on any axis, which would mean the built-form reader is matching nothing and the green is vacuous; (b) a built surface on which the artboard reader and the built reader both match, which would mean the two forms are not distinguishable and the exclusivity self-tests are wrong; (c) a Parks surface carrying a table, a data-metric tile or any built-surface vocabulary term, or an invented state word outside the design's badge set; (d) a roster count on the page disagreeing with DOMAIN_REGISTRY, or a parks entry appearing in DOMAIN_REGISTRY - the second would make every sentence on the page false; (e) a vendor gate or a counted figure on the surface ('gatedBy X' or a 24px data-font number), which is the built-surface shape; (f) a near miss used as content rather than named as not-this-lens; (g) the composer sentence appearing paraphrased rather than verbatim, or the page quoting a refusal wording the product no longer throws; (h) any of the three parks-facilities probes ceasing to refuse; (i) a lens route answering 200 on a deployed app today - that would mean a deploy happened that this close says did not.

LESSON: A ROW WHOSE DELIVERABLE IS A NEGATIVE CLAIM NEEDS ITS INSTRUMENT TO BE ABLE TO SAY 'NO' TWICE. This surface is only correct if the built-surface vocabulary is absent AND the absence reasons are present, and those are two different predicates pointing in opposite directions. An instrument that only refused vocabulary would pass an empty page; one that only required reasons would pass a page that also invented a tile. The design's Main/Difference split is exactly that pair, which is why the row could be built at all.

A PAGE CAN QUOTE THE PRODUCT AND STILL LIE TOMORROW. The composer sentence and the three refusal messages are taken from the running modules (the refusals are RE-FIRED at import, not copied into a string), so the page cannot keep citing a wording the product has stopped using. Copying them would have been correct on the day it shipped and silently wrong afterwards - the same failure mode as a fixture anchored to a date.

AN ATTRIBUTE THAT EXISTS TO LET AN INSTRUMENT SCOPE A DOCUMENT MUST NOT SHIP IN THE PRODUCT'S OWN SHELL. data-lens-body="parks" is what makes check.mjs able to read the surface document; the shipped web/index.html must NOT carry it, or the instrument's handle has leaked into the product. The suite asserts both directions: present in the served page, absent in the shell.

THE EDGE HEADER PROVES THE SUBSTRATE, NOT THE APP. x-do-app-origin + x-do-orig-status prove an App Platform app issued the status; they do not name it, and on this fleet the origin ids do not match the app ids the API returns. A lane that reported 'the edge header proves dolphin-app answered' would have been stating something the header cannot carry - so the app is identified by the domain binding in its own spec and both facts are recorded.

A PROBE THAT CANNOT REACH THE NETWORK MUST SAY WHICH SIDE FAILED. The first run of this lane's probe recorded 'fetch failed' for every deployed row because Node could not verify the chain without the system trust store. That is a refusal about the probe, not about the app, and the artifact now says so on the row rather than reporting the app as down.
DEAD-END: Running the lane's HTTP probe without --use-system-ca: every deployed row reads 'fetch failed' and a reader could mistake a trust-store problem for an outage. Provenance and hint are now recorded per row.

Probing /lens/parks with ?cityKey=bastrop_tx to measure reachability: bastrop_tx is tenant-private, so an anonymous read is 401 BY DESIGN and the probe would have reported 'the route does not serve the lens'. The 200 is read on a public-free pack (template-city) and 401/404 are kept as their own control rows.
Pointing the existing artboard readers at built markup (the g152 dead end, re-confirmed here): they match zero, and a zero-matched green is indistinguishable from a pass.

Editing the design instrument's predicates to reach exit 0. The instrument gained an additive reader instead; its predicates and its two-sided rule are untouched and its new self-tests assert the two readers cannot see each other's form.
